turns.prompt_text: In the Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, I am in the early game and I'm trying to get a coat so I can go into the cold areas. However, to do that, I need to hunt down a wild boar for the raw meat. I am having trouble finding spawn locations.
turns.response_html:
That hunting quest on the Great Plateau can be incredibly frustrating. Those boars are notoriously skittish, and if you run or make too much noise nearby, they will bolt and de-spawn into the trees before you even see them.

The exact creature you are looking for is the Woodland Boar, and they have a very specific home base on the starting plateau.

Best Spawn Location: The Forest of Spirits

The absolute best place to find them is the Forest of Spirits, which is the dense, wooded area located in the northern section of the Great Plateau (just northwest of the Temple of Time).

  • Where they hang out: They tend to spawn deep among the trees, often near the roots of large oaks or foraging in small clearings.
  • The Reset Trick: If you accidentally scare them away, they won't immediately pop back up. The easiest fix is to fast-travel to the Oman Au Shrine (the Magnesis shrine just outside the woods) or the Great Plateau Tower, then walk back into the forest. This resets the local wildlife spawns.

Tips for a Successful Hunt

Because their line of sight and hearing are so sharp, standard hunting tactics usually fail. Try this approach instead:

  1. Crouch and Move Slow: Press down on the left joystick to click into a crouch. Only move when the sound indicator (the purple wave graphic on the bottom right of your HUD) stays low.
  2. Go for a Headshot: Boars have a high health pool for early-game bows. A body shot with a basic traveler's bow won't kill them, and they will run away. Aim directly for the snout/head for a one-shot critical kill.
  3. Use the Environment: If sneaking is taking too long, climb one of the large trees in the forest and look down into the clearings. You can easily spot their dark brown shapes moving through the grass and take your shot from safety without triggering their sound detection.

Once you take one down, grab the Raw Meat and combine it with a Hyrule Herb and a Spicy Pepper at the Old Man's cooking pot to cook up that Spicy Meat and Seafood Fry!

turns.prompt_text: That makes sense. The problem I've been having is I've just been running around the forest and then I wait till morning at the campfire and then I do another loop or three around the entire forest again. Sometimes I climb up a tree and look around, but I am unable to find them. And oftentimes, I'll just walk right into one and it'll knock me over and run away. But once it's running away, I can never catch them.
turns.response_html:
That exact loop is incredibly punishing because of how Breath of the Wild handles animal spawns and AI awareness. Running around the forest actually works against you, and passing time at a campfire doesn't automatically drop a boar right next to you.

Here is exactly why that strategy is running into a wall, and how to change up your approach so you can finally get that meat.

Why the "Forest Loops" Are Tricking You

  • Passing Time Doesn't Reset Spawns: Sitting at a campfire to advance the clock passes the time, but it doesn't force the game to aggressively reload the area's wildlife if you are still standing right there.
  • The Render Distance Trap: If you are running loops, you are moving faster than the time it takes to spot them. By the time a boar's 3D model actually loads into the brush ahead of you, your running footsteps have already triggered its "flee" AI.
  • The Aggressive Blindside: When you accidentally walk right into one and get knocked over, it means you caught it completely by surprise while moving fast. Once they are running, do not chase them. Link's early-game sprint speed is significantly slower than a panicked boar, and they are hardcoded to sprint straight out of bounds or vanish into thick brush once spooked.

Try the "Drop-In" Method Instead

Instead of pacing back and forth on the forest floor, use a method that lets you use vertical space and forces the game to fresh-spawn the wildlife.

Alternative Option: If the Forest of Spirits is giving you too much trouble, there is a single Woodland Boar that occasionally spawns on the snowy slopes just north of the River of the Dead near the waterfall. However, you'll need to eat some Spicy Peppers just to survive the walk over there to look for it!

turns.prompt_text: In Breath of the Wild, if I have less clothes on, do I run faster? Does it help me at all? Same with a shield and a bow and a sword.
turns.response_html:
It feels like it should make you faster—stripping off heavy armor to run light is a classic gaming trope. However, in Breath of the Wild, taking off your clothes does not make you run or sprint any faster.

Link's base movement speed is identical whether he is wearing a full set of heavy soldier's armor, his starting trousers, or absolutely nothing at all.

That said, your equipment does affect stealth, stamina, and sound in very specific ways. Here is exactly how your gear interacts with your movement:

1. Armor, Clothes, and the Naked Stealth Myth

While being naked won't make you faster, wearing nothing actually makes you quieter than wearing heavy metal armor.

  • The Noise Factor: Every piece of armor has a hidden "noise weight." Heavy metal armor (like the Soldier's Set you find later) clanks loudly, making your sound indicator spike even when walking.
  • The Naked Benefit: Stripping down minimizes your default movement noise. However, it is not as effective as wearing dedicated stealth gear (like the Stealth Set from Kakariko Village), which actively dampens your footsteps beyond base levels.
  • The Cold Problem: Right now on the Great Plateau, taking your clothes off will actually actively hurt you because it removes any baseline defense and makes you incredibly vulnerable to environmental cold or enemy attacks.

2. Weapons, Shields, and Bows (The "Weight" Rules)

Having swords, shields, and bows equipped on your back does not slow down your running speed or drain your stamina faster. You can carry pages and pages of heavy claymores in your inventory, and Link will still sprint at maximum speed.

However, having your weapon actively drawn in your hands changes things:

Action / StateImpact on Movement & Stamina
Gear on your backZero penalty. Sprinting and running are at maximum efficiency.
One-Handed Weapon DrawnLink can run and maneuver normally, but cannot sprint without putting it away.
Two-Handed Weapon DrawnLink's movement slows down slightly while the weapon is unsheathed, and swinging it drains stamina rapidly.
Shield Raised (Z-Targeting)You drop into a defensive strafe. You move much slower, but it keeps your guard up.
Drawing a BowSlows you down to a walking pace while aiming.

How to Actually Move Faster

If you want to speed up your loops or outrun wildlife, you have to use the game's actual speed mechanics rather than modifying your clothing layout:

  • Speed Food/Elixirs: Cook items with Fleet-Lotus Seeds, Swift Carrots, or Rushaush (found later in the game) to get a "Haste" buff. This actively increases your running, climbing, and swimming speeds by up to 30%.
  • The Sheikah Set: Later on, buying the full Stealth Set and upgrading it twice at a Great Fairy grants a Night Speed Up bonus, making you run significantly faster automatically between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM.

Keep your clothes on for the defense and cold resistance—if you want to get the jump on those boars, rely on clicking that left joystick to crouch rather than stripping down!
